clusters.text: The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean as it burst into flames SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday. It is the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:45 local time (22:45 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead, it has splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it is in space. If any problems are detected, there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. clusters.text: Former opener Warner was banned for a year for his involvement in the 2018 ‘Sandpapergate’ incident in South Africa. David Warner blasted Cricket Australia’s handling of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal as “a cover-up” on Saturday, escalating a row that has torn apart the sport. Former opener Warner, who was banned for a year over his part in the “ Sandpapergate ” incident in Cape Town, lashed out at what he claimed was “a shoddy investigation”. “As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation,” he said on Instagram. “If that’s correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know? “It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose, and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea. Festering wounds over what happened in the third Test at Cape Town were reopened this week when Usman Khawaja released his autobiography. In the book, he alleged that the whole team knew about the plot to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing. A Cricket Australia probe concluded that only then-skipper Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft were in the know, with all three sent home from South Africa in disgrace . Starc, Hazlewood, Lyon and Pat Cummins all denied publicly in a 2021 statement that they were aware of the plan. On Friday, Cummins, now the Test captain, held a lengthy news conference to rubbish Khawaja’s latest claims, calling them “ 100 percent wrong “. In response, Warner accused him of throwing close friend Khawaja “under the bus”. Starc also stated during the week that “we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field”. Hazlewood and Lyon have yet to comment. Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening their investigation and, in a statement on Saturday, said all players had been given the chance to come forward. “As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since,” a spokesperson said. “Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players’ right to provide their own version of events.”

clusters.text: The Pope, who has Peruvian citizenship, lived in Chiclayo for several years Pope Leo XIV has celebrated Mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago . Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the Mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C. For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight. "The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth Díaz, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023. Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff , who was elected in May 2025. The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance. The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities. clusters.text: GTA 6 will feature brand new protagonists Jason and Lucia - the first playable female character in any of the 3D games After a 13-year wait, two delays, and several high-profile leaks , the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is fast approaching. The next chapter in the nearly 30-year-old series, where players explore open worlds and break the law, has created an extraordinary level of anticipation. And with developer Rockstar Games keeping their biggest release yet, tightly under wraps, even the people who helped bring the original to life aren't getting special treatment. "We're all waiting to see what they've done," Dave Jones, GTA's co-creator, tells me, sitting alongside the original game's writer and publicist, Brian Baglow. Have either of them been able to play the new game ahead of launch? Baglow shakes his head. He's not complaining, though. "I've got the pre-order," he says. Brian Baglow (left) and Dave Jones, worked on the original Grand Theft Auto The original Grand Theft Auto was released in 1997 in Dundee, Scotland by DMA Design, a relatively small team, at least judging by later games' standards. Following its success with puzzle game Lemmings, the studio was toying around with the idea of making a racing game, initially called Race'n'Chase. Sitting in the state-of-the-art computer lab at Dundee's Abertay University decades on, Jones tells me the developers still felt they had to bring something new to the table. "At DMA, we always wanted to do something different," he says. "What was the unique spin we could put on it?" Part of the answer, he said, came in what feels like a premise gamers take for granted now - "just getting out of the car". He says the idea of being able to not only drive but switch and steal cars, running about on foot as you did so, meant "all of a sudden you had this interesting mix of gaming coming together". clusters.text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday laid out a multi-tier blueprint for how India was navigating an increasingly fractured global order, asserting that India must make up for lost ground in traditional manufacturing while racing ahead in frontier technologies.The minister said domestic economic initiatives such as Atmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, were not merely economic policies, but "the building blocks of a foreign policy."He was speaking to R Sukumar, Editor-in-Chief, Hindustan Times, at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi. The theme of this year's summit is "New Rules. New Realities."Jaishankar said India had laid a very solid foundation over the last decade but stressed that it had "missed the manufacturing bus" in the past. Jaishankar pointed to the period from the 1960s to the 1990s as "lost decades," noting that even the 1991–92 reforms served only as a "partial correction." To close that gap today, he highlighted the role of schemes such as the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) in kickstarting neglected sectors and boosting small and medium enterprises (SMEs), backed by aggressive upgrades in physical infrastructure and logistics.To remain competitive in the contemporary era, Jaishankar stressed that India must simultaneously invest in next-generation strategic pillars; scale up domestic capabilities in semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), and bio-life sciences, and expand educational institutions and vocational skilling to prepare the workforce for an AI-driven economy.Speaking in the context of the shifting currents of global geopolitics, Jaishankar said, traditional alliances would become "less cohesive" and "more transactional," giving rise to a sharper, more self-centred competition among nations.“It calls really for much stronger capacities at home. clusters.text: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows its AI agents, known as dots, to complete purchases on behalf of users after receiving their approval. The feature marks an expansion of ChatGPT's shopping capabilities, moving beyond product discovery and recommendations to facilitating transactions. The service is initially being rolled out to a limited group of ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US who are at least 18 years old and hold eligible US-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express cards. Under the new system, users can add their payment cards to ChatGPT Wallet once and authorise their dots to use them when making purchases. Before a transaction is completed, users will be shown the selected products, the final amount and the card chosen for payment. They must then confirm the transaction through a security measure such as Face ID or fingerprint authentication. OpenAI said the system uses payment tokens to process transactions. These tokens act as substitutes for actual card information and include the details required to complete a payment. This means the user's original card details are not disclosed to either the AI agent or the merchant. Once a transaction is authorised, the merchant receives the information required to process and deliver the order, including the customer's shipping address and contact details. Card rewards and protections to continue OpenAI said customers using ChatGPT Wallet will retain their existing credit card rewards and applicable consumer protections. These include the ability to dispute eligible transactions, such as purchases involving defective products. The company has developed the payment feature in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. It said banks and payment networks will continue to play a role in assessing transactions, while merchants will retain control over pricing, order fulfilment, returns and customer service. OpenAI plans wider agent-led shopping capabilities The initial rollout will allow OpenAI to assess how the wallet performs in actual shopping situations and improve its compatibility with merchants, banks and payment networks. clusters.text: Ranchi: The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) have deployed teams in Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Deoghar and Hazaribag districts to prevent incidents of drowning at the Chhath ghats, its deputy commandant Vinay Kumar said on Friday.Lakhs of devotees are expected to gather at ponds, river banks and other waterbodies across the state to offer their prayers to the setting and rising sun on Nov 15 and Nov 16.A NDRF team comprises 30 members who were experts in various facets of rescue operations, including deep diving. “The teams will patrol Chhath ghats and ensure devotees do not cross barricades erected by the local administration to keep them within safe zones,” a NDRF official in Ranchi said, requesting anonymity. The teams will carry lifebuoys, which will be thrown to anyone suspected of drowning. Deep divers will be pressed into service if a victim sinks below the water.Sources said NDRF usually functions as a full 30-member unit, but in Deoghar it has been split into two groups and posted at two ponds.In Ranchi, a NDRF teams will be deployed at Dhurwa Dam while a state disaster response force team will be deployed at Vivekananda Sarovar (Ranchi Lake). “Officials have also been directed to arrange additional divers for other ponds that draw large crowds,” Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said. These divers will remain deployed from Sunday afternoon to Monday afternoon will be shared with administrative and police officials for faster coordination during any emergency.Signages have been placed at 260 waterbodies across the district where the water is deep, warning devotees against venturing beyond barricaded limits during rituals and offering prayers.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. clusters.title: Andreeva sweeps WTA Finals group losing just 11 games, brushing aside stand-in Shnaider
clusters.snippet: Mirra Andreeva beat alternate Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes to complete a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells: three wins, six sets, 11 games dropped. She faces Jessica Pegula in the semi-finals on Saturday.
clusters.text: Mirra Andreeva beat alternate Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes to complete a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells: three wins, six sets, 11 games dropped. She faces Jessica Pegula in the semi-finals on Saturday. Mirra Andreeva completed a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Friday. The third seed beat her compatriot and doubles partner Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes, and ends Group 2 with three wins, six sets won and only 11 games dropped. Andreeva converted six of her seven break points against Shnaider, who had stepped in as second alternate after Karolina Muchova withdrew with gastrointestinal issues. The 19-year-old now leads their head-to-head 3-0. Already sure of first place in the group after her wins over Elina Svitolina and Aryna Sabalenka, both 6-4, 6-0, Andreeva will face Jessica Pegula in the first semi-final on Saturday, a week after the American was caught on a hot mic calling her “a diva”. A third group win is worth another 200 points, which takes Andreeva to 6,906 points in the live rankings, 221 ahead of Sabalenka. The Belarusian, later knocked out by Svitolina 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 , can no longer catch her: Andreeva will be world No. 2 on Monday. Shnaider, making her WTA Finals debut, leaves with $230,000 for her one match, on top of the $100,000 she received as an alternate.

clusters.title: Housing restrictions ease with govt’s nod to Master Plan amendments
clusters.text: Prayagraj: Restrictions on group housing and multi-storey buildings in Civil Lines, Georgetown and Tagore Town may be lifted after the state govt’s approval to the amendments to the Prayagraj Master Plan-2031. The Prayagraj Development Authority (PDA) has invited public objections and suggestions before the changes are implemented..The restrictions imposed under Master Plan-2031 had led to difficulties for residents and developers in these areas. Taking note of the problems, PDA had sent a proposal to govt seeking amendments to remove the restrictions which the govt has no approved.Residents and other stakeholders can submit their objections and suggestions in writing, addressed to the PDA vice-chairman, in three copies. Only objections and suggestions received within 15 days from the date of publication of the notice will be considered.Under the proposed amendment, construction will be permitted on residential plots measuring less than 200 square metres in Civil Lines, Georgetown and Tagore Town, subject to approval of building maps by PDA. The amendment will also allow residential buildings to exceed the earlier maximum permissible height of 7.50 metres.The move is also expected to revive several group housing projects stalled due to the restrictions. Several builders had submitted applications to PDA for group housing and multi-storey projects in Civil Lines, Georgetown and Tagore Town. However, with the master plan prohibiting such construction, the applications remained pending.The proposed amendment may increase the availability of housing options in some of the city’s established residential localities and provide prospective homebuyers with more choices.PDA is expected to proceed with the amendment after examining the objections and suggestions received during the stipulated period.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news.
